newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TYSON FACES LIKELY SUSPENSION, OFFICIAL SAYS.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TYSON FACES LIKELY SUSPENSION, OFFICIAL SAYS.

text.p: A member of the Nevada Athletic Commission that will decide on discipline against Mike Tyson said on Tuesday the boxer would probably be suspended for biting Evander Holyfield's ears during a title fight.

Luther Mack, one of five members of the commission that will discipline Tyson, told ABC's "Good Morning America": "We can suspend him because what he did was not tolerated ... certainly we would do something in that area -- exactly in terms of months, years at this point in time, I do not know."

Holyfield's attorney, speaking on the same television programme, said his client, the heavyweight champion, accepted an apology made by Tyson but he wanted the commission to preserve the integrity of boxing.
The commission is due to meet later on Tuesday to decide what action should be taken against Tyson after he bit both of the champion's ears in a heavyweight title fight on Saturday in Las Vegas.
The fight was stopped in the third round and Tyson disqualified after he ignored a warning from the referee.
Among its options, the commission could fine, suspend or ban Tyson from the sport. It could also revoke his boxing license.
Tyson held a news conference on Monday, apologised for "snapping" in the ring and begged for forgiveness.
He said he would accept the commission's punishment but asked only that it not be a lifetime ban from boxing.
Holyfield's attorney, Jim Thomas, said while his fighter accepted the apology, he wanted the commission to take "meaningful" sanctions that would preserve the sport's integrity.
"He (Holyfield) certainly accepts the apology and hopes that it's sincere," Thomas said in the same "Good Morning America" interview.

"He doesn't have any personal desire to hurt or punish Mike Tyson ... Evander wants something done that will help preserve the integrity of that sport, and for that to happen some very meaningful sanctions need to be issued by the commission."
